ety.text: Hindi verb set जगना (jagnā) जागना (jāgnā) जगाना (jagānā) जगवाना (jagvānā) Inherited from Prakrit जग्गइ (jaggaï), from older जग्गति (jaggati), from Sanskrit जाग्रति (jāgrati), a later variant of जागर्ति (jāgarti), the intensive from the root गृ (gṛ, “to wake”). Compare Punjabi ਜਾਗਣਾ (jāgṇā) / جاگنا (jāgnā), Gujarati જાગવું (jāgvũ), Nepali जाग्नु (jāgnu), Sindhi جَاڳَڻُ (jāg̠aṇu) / जाॻणु (jāɡ̈aṇu), Bengali জাগা (jaga), Assamese জাগা (zaga), Marathi जागणे (j̈āgṇe), Konkani जाग्चे (zāgce). More distantly related to Classical Persian بیدَار (bēdār), whence Hindi बेदार (bedār, “awake”).
Compare Classical Persian تَکْیَه کَلَام (takya kalām, “slogan”).

ety.text: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *swenh₂- Proto-Indo-Iranian *swanH- Sanskrit स्वन् (svan) Sanskrit स्वनति (svanati) Proto-New Indo-Aryan *सणइ (saṇaï) Hindi सनकना Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *सणइ (saṇaï) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓𑁆𑀓- (-kka-), from Sanskrit स्वनति (svanati, “it sounds”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *swenh₂-.
